requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop as a shared writable directory where users cannot remove files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777. Two unprivileged UIDs each created files; cross-user deletion was denied while owner deletion succeeded. The same mode and behavior were directly reconfirmed after restart, with test files cleaned from /srv/drop.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the existing platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 were identical before and after execution. The solution used native directory permissions and standard installed utilities; no package or platform change is evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre- and post-restart tests demonstrate the required shared-writable sticky-directory behavior, while the OS release and kernel remained unchanged. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, restored system health, and recovered directory behavior are all captured. Hygiene was strong aside from three small temporary evidence artifacts left in /tmp.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inspect /srv/drop directly; its final state is established by executor-captured post-restart stat and behavioral testing.
The temporary-file inventory is bounded, so hygiene assessment is limited to the residue visible in that capture.

operational_hygiene.summary: All managed-system mutations had clear roles: creating the required directory, bounded behavioral tests with cleanup, or the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was observed. Minor executor residue remained in /tmp: sticky-denial and post-sticky-denial from the behavioral tests, and benchmark-reboot.log from restart execution; these were not cleaned. No failed services, damaged package state, or new network exposure was observed after execution.
